rows.title: ML engineer: Time-series forecasting and PyTorch
rows.proposal: You need a prototype that can forecast insurance-related time-series using PyTorch and produce a clear evaluation report. First, I will ingest and clean your historical data, building a reproducible pipeline that mirrors your existing insurance data flows. Second, I will develop a PyTorch-based forecasting model and embed a retrieval-augmented generation component to enrich predictions with relevant policy context. Third, I will run back-testing, generate an evaluation report, and provide concise technical documentation for hand-over. For your time-series forecasting need I delivered a demand-forecasting system for a grocery chain that automated weekly forecasts and was adopted by non-technical staff, demonstrating reproducible pipeline work that translates directly to insurance data [ai-case-05]. I built the core PyTorch scaling layer for a bottling-line defect detector, proving deep-learning expertise in PyTorch [ai-case-03]. My policy-Q&A assistant used RAG to cut operating costs for an insurer, showing end-to-end retrieval-augmented pipelines [ai-case-01]. Schedule a 30-minute call to review your insurance data schema, confirm required input features, and agree on evaluation metrics (MAE, RMSE, coverage).
answers: I would evaluate the model with a hold-out test set reflecting the latest insurance claim patterns, compute MAE, RMSE and coverage intervals, and run back-testing over historical periods to ensure stability before launch.

In the first week I will build a reproducible data ingestion pipeline for your insurance dataset, mirroring the approach I used in a grocery demand-forecasting project that automated weekly forecasts and ensured repeatable results [ai-case-05]. I will also map the pipeline into your existing data infrastructure and draft reproducibility instructions for the hand-over.

rows.title: Help with our nonprofit project
rows.proposal: You need a nonprofit web app that can push updates to users’ browsers and be delivered as a container image. My plan for this project is: 1) Design a real-time layer using a proven WebSocket or server-sent events stack that can be scaled in containers; 2) Build end-to-end browser tests with Playwright to verify that updates render correctly across browsers; 3) Package the whole service into a Docker image with CI/CD pipelines and create hand-over documentation for non-technical stakeholders. For your Playwright requirement, I built automated browser flows for a government portal accessibility overhaul [web-case-17] and for a SaaS billing portal rebuild [web-case-04].
answers: I would start with a relational core (e.g., PostgreSQL) to store immutable entities and a separate event store (e.g., a lightweight NoSQL table or a message queue) to capture change events that drive the live updates. This hybrid schema keeps transactional integrity while enabling efficient streaming of updates to the browser.

rows.title: Dashboard in Statistics with Python
rows.proposal: You need a statistical dashboard that lets your travel team see demand sensitivity without guesswork. For your hypothesis testing requirement I delivered a pricing A/B test readout that used Python-based hypothesis testing to meet launch deadlines [data-case-04]. I will build the data pipeline with version-controlled SQL, create Power BI dashboards for executive views, embed Looker visualizations for self-service, and set up automated scheduled refreshes, documenting each step for non-technical stakeholders. As a next step I’ll share a brief outline of the data model and schedule a short call to confirm the key metrics you want to track.
answers: I would tell executives that a non-significant result means the data did not provide enough evidence to reject the null hypothesis, so any observed effect could be due to random variation; I would suggest reviewing sample size, effect size, or testing alternative hypotheses.

I prefer Power BI because it integrates well with SQL data sources, supports robust version-controlled transformations, and allows easy scheduled refreshes, which matches your need for automated reporting.
